summary: Brick-and-stucco light of 1896 at the Coquille River mouth in Bullards Beach State Park; automated in 1939, leased to the state as a park in 1963.

structures.note: Attached to the fog-signal building (USLHS); LF calls it cylindrical

access.note: Park grounds open; signal room open in season with volunteers; tower closed to the public (Oregon State Parks).

facts.agency: Oregon Parks and Recreation Department (Oregon State Parks)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS records a conical tower attached to the signal building. LF describes a cylindrical tower joined to an octagonal fog-signal room. The NRHP nomination describes stuccoed brick walls without naming the shape. The shape is recorded as the archive gives it, with LF's description noted.

The Oregon State Parks page says the Coast Guard built the lighthouse in 1896. The Light-House Board's annual reports for 1891 to 1896 describe the construction under the Lighthouse Board. The Board's reports are followed here.

The NRHP nomination says 1939, when an automated light on the south jetty succeeded it. LF says the Coast Guard assumed responsibility and decided the light was no longer needed in 1939. The date agrees; the reason is LF's.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination (1973) is digitised and read in full; it is the main source for the 1939, 1963 and 1974 dates. Board volumes 1891-1901 are in the local corpus. Scan pages were checked against the Internet Archive: 578, 233 and 547 by the corpus OCR page index; 196, 455, 248, 260 and 397 (FY1895) by the in-item search; 203 (the 1896 fog list) from the XML page index, calibrated on the in-item results for the same volume (196 and 455). Two citations rest on the XML page index only, because the archive.org in-item search returned errors: scan page 220 (FY1900 storm, annualreportlig00statgoog) and scan page 51 (Life-Saving Service 1892 loss, annualreportope09servgoog). Check the page images before publishing. The Commissioner volume's pages (85, 264, 457, 551, 756) were checked against its OCR page index. The 1936 Bulletin text is column-scrambled OCR; the Rose sentences follow page 39. The 1930 fog figure is the Bulletin's report for the fiscal year 1929. LF says Langlois and Walters were commended for helping refugees; no primary record for that commendation was found. The record's characteristic QY is not confirmed: LF describes a fixed white light with an occulting shutter (28 seconds of light, 2 seconds of eclipse), so the characteristic may need review. Whether the Marie Langlois of 1925 is the Marie Amundsen whom LF names as Oscar R. Langlois's wife is not established by any source; no link is claimed. The Life-Saving station at the river mouth (us-or-coquille-river-life-boat-station) has its own record; the 1892 loss is cited here only because it happened at the same river mouth. The Board's 1891-1901 keeper rosters are not in the corpus; the USLHS roster matches LF's list line for line. Disagreement: Oregon State Parks says the lighthouse was 'built by the U.S. Coast Guard in 1896'; the Board's reports for 1891-1896 record its construction under the Board. The story follows the Board's reports and states the disagreement.
